author: DTrim99
body:
PolicyEngine did apply the worksheet's income offset — the difference is *which* percentage schedule, which turns on who the Schedule H claimant is.

Both sides agree on the inputs: 20% × 14,690.78 rent = 2,938.16, and unit AGI 52,382. The TaxAct Schedule H names the primary filer (DOB 1/1/1956, age 65) as claimant, so its worksheet uses the under-70 table's 5% band for AGI $52,000–56,200: 2,938 − 2,619 = 319. PolicyEngine treats the unit as senior because the spouse is 73: the 3% senior band (D.C. Code §47-1806.06(a)(2A), income limit $76,700 in 2021) gives 2,938.16 − 1,571.47 = 1,366.69, capped at the $1,225 maximum. So the 1,225 is the capped senior computation rather than a skipped phaseout.

On the law, §47-1806.06(b)(9) keys the senior schedule to "a claimant who is 70 years or older," and (b)(4) defines the claimant as any member of the tax filing unit who was an owner or a lessee paying rent for the full year — one claimant per unit, but not necessarily the primary filer. A couple in this position would designate the 73-year-old as claimant and receive 1,225, which is why we lean toward the either-spouse-70+ reading. Does taxsimtest key Schedule H to the primary filer's age (page) only, or to the older of page/sage? If you treat the primary-claimant convention as authoritative we can switch the model, but the claimant-optimization reading seems closer to how a preparer would file this couple.

Everything else on the record reconciles: D-40 tax before credits 1,274.93 on taxable 24,582, and PE's siitax 49.93 = 1,274.93 − 1,225.

Example household:
